problem: SHAE-5 found that this repository's Codex gate had the same defects as the relay. F-1 (medium): a Codex review WITH findings publishes its completion receipt as a pull-request review, but scripts/review-budget.mjs and scripts/promote-reviewed-pr.mjs only read issue comments, so the repair-review cycle stalls at previous_review_pending. F-2 (low): a valid CODEX_REVIEW_REQUEST_TOKEN that belongs to the wrong GitHub user returned skipped_wrong_requester and the run was green. F-3 (low-medium): the readiness workflow used one repo-wide concurrency group, so a pending run for one PR could be dropped when another PR's run queued. A fourth defect found during SHAE-13: scripts/review-budget.mjs only read literal [P0]-[P3] markers, but Codex states priority as a rendered badge (![P0 Badge](...)), so every real finding read as P1. A P0 would not stop for the owner and P2/P3 findings were held to the looser P1 cap. Fixing F-1 makes this reachable, because findings-round receipts become visible to the loop.
solution: F-1: review-budget.mjs gains codexReceipt and classifyCodexReview. A receipt is accepted from the Codex bot as an issue comment (clean review) or a submitted PR review (review with findings), only if commit_id equals the exact head and the body has the receipt marker and a Reviewed commit prefix of that head. The request script reads GET /pulls/{n}/reviews after a prior request exists (incomplete scans fail closed) and the ready gate promotes only a clean classification. Budget caps, P0 stop, CI and hold rules are unchanged. F-2: a wrong-owner token now throws codex_request_wrong_requester; the CLI exits 1 with a fixed ::error annotation that never prints a login or token, posts nothing and leaves the PR a draft. F-3: the PR-creation job was already per branch (agent-pr-<branch>); the readiness gate group is now per PR for a Codex comment and one shared group for sweeps, and the sparse checkout adds scripts/review-budget.mjs, which the gate now imports. Docs updated. Severity parser: findingsForSha now reads priority from the first line in both the rendered badge and literal-marker forms, ported from Agent Relay. If a line carries conflicting markers (e.g. badge alt text vs image URL, or a badge plus a bracket marker) the MOST severe wins, so a lower marker cannot hide a P0. No marker stays P1; below the first line only a P0 counts (it escalates, as the old match-anywhere rule did) and lower markers there are ignored; only Codex-authored findings for the exact commit count. P0 escalation, the 5/3/1 severity caps, global limit, no-progress stop, receipt verification and owner merge are unchanged.
tests: npm ci: ok. npm run check (lint, format:check, typecheck, vitest, build, package:check, build-storybook): exit 0; vitest 689 passed in 55 files, publint and consumer smoke test passed, Storybook built (401 entries)

node --test request-codex-review, review-budget, promote-reviewed-pr, review-gate-trigger and sync-linear-lifecycle test files: 88 passed, 0 failed. Baseline on main for the first four files was 33 passed.

Severity parser tests (review-budget.test.mjs, 26 pass): all four levels in 8 first-line forms, one fingerprint across forms, 8 ambiguous-marker cases resolve to the most severe, a P0 on a later line still escalates while lower markers there are ignored, malformed shapes default to P1 without throwing, non-Codex and wrong-commit findings ignored.

P0 escalation (request-codex-review.test.mjs, 29 pass): a P0 in 7 forms, via issue-comment and PR-review receipts, ends in a REVIEW HOLD (critical_finding, P0) with no @codex review posted; no App token stops loudly; an already-held PR is never re-requested.

Budgets preserved: badge-form P3 holds after 2 rounds, P2 after 4, P2 within its cap still requests, P1 allows 5 then the global limit; no-progress works across badge and literal forms; receipts, stale SHA and duplicate-request denials unchanged.

Mutation checks: 10 deliberate regressions (old parser, least-severe-wins, image level ignored, P0 hold removed, P0 downgraded to P1, any-author findings, unmarked as P3, markers beyond line 1, any-commit findings, later-line P0 ignored) each made a named test fail; the file was restored. Earlier F-1/F-2/F-3 mutation checks are unchanged.

NOT run: GitHub Actions itself and actionlint (the workflow edit takes effect after merge), and a live UI review with findings; this parser is proven against the badge text observed on Relay PR #27, not on a UI PR.
risks: HIGH-RISK PATH: edits .github/workflows/promote-reviewed-agent-pr.yml (protected), proven by static tests only, so watch the first post-merge run; a bad sparse checkout would stop every PR from becoming ready. The receipt reader and severity parser trust only Codex-authored evidence for the exact commit and never lower a clean-review, CI or hold requirement. Parser behavior change: P2/P3 badge findings now reach their own caps (3/1) instead of the P1 cap (5), so holds can come sooner than before; a marker anywhere in the first line counts, even inside an HTML comment, so doubtful input errs toward escalation. A comment with no first-line marker is still P1. A comment run and a sweep can overlap for one PR; the gate rechecks draft state and head before the ready mutation. This is a SHAE operational branch; UICOMP lifecycle sync will not update SHAE-13.
